summary: A list of RFCs by number, dated August 1, 1971, giving each document's first author, title, date and NIC and RFC numbers. It extends earlier lists such as RFC 170 and RFC 160 and was a tool for finding documents.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 200 is an index of RFCs issued through August 1971. Its table gives each listed document's author, title, date, and catalogue numbers so readers can locate it.

subtitle: An August 1971 index listing the author, title, date, NIC number, and RFC number.

tldr.problem: Readers needed a way to find documents in the growing RFC series.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 200 presents a table ordered by RFC number, with each entry's first author, title, date, NIC number, and RFC number.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 160 and RFC 170 and records the series through RFC 200.

sections.title: An Index by RFC Number
sections.content:
RFC 200 is titled RFC List by Number, dated August 1, 1971, and carries NIC number 7152. The author is listed as unknown.

The document is a table rather than a protocol description. It obsoletes the earlier lists RFC 160 and RFC 170.
sections.plainLanguage: This document is a table that helps readers find earlier RFCs. It updates two earlier lists.

sections.title: Information in Each Entry
sections.content:
Each table entry identifies the first author, document title, date, NIC number, and RFC number. Longer titles continue on another line.

The NIC number and RFC number are separate identifiers. For example, RFC 1 is listed with NIC number 4687.
sections.plainLanguage: Each row gives two different catalogue numbers along with the document's author, name, and date. The NIC number is not the RFC number.

sections.title: Gaps and Revisions in the List
sections.content:
The entries begin with RFC 1, dated 7 April 1969, and continue through RFC 200. The topics listed include host software, file transfer, TELNET, and network graphics.

Some numbers are marked as never issued, and RFC 137 appears with a revision entry. The final note says the list was converted to machine-readable form for the online archives in March 1998.
sections.plainLanguage: The index records early network documents and shows that some numbers were unused. It also marks a revision and notes when the list was added to the online archives.
